messages:
sophie: heads-up — noticed a bunch of requests showing up under the org key in the console even though customers are using project-scoped keys. console UI is showing project X, but billing/quotas attributed to org-default. anyone else seeing this?
aj: yep saw that in the cost dashboard earlier, thought it was a sampling glitch. can you paste a request-id?
sophie: > req=01FZ9K9Q2QWR7P4A0ZZ0XYZ
leah: ops-bot alerted on quota bump for org-default ~3h ago. i pulled trace for that req id, the auth header had `x-origin: project:X` but the auth resolver returned no project claim. it fell back to `org:org-123`.
aj: that matches a recent change — we added a permissive fallback when project claim parsing fails to avoid hard rejects. fallback routing currently prioritizes (project, org, org-default) but if project claim missing we rewrite to org-default.
nate: do we know why project claim was missing? token was issued by our console for project X, right?
leah: token looks fine in issuer DB. hypothesis: edge proxy strips `x-project` header for multi-part requests when body is multipart/form-data. seen similar in file upload paths.
sophie: ugh. so console shows project X (from client) but request attribution goes to org-default — bad for tenant isolation and quotas. we need a quick mitigation + longer term fix.
aj: short-term: revert permissive fallback -> return 400 if no project claim and request indicates project in header. that'll fail a few customers but prevents silent leak to org quota. can gate behind feature-flag `auth.strict_project_claims`.
nate: agree — roll canary to 5% of traffic on staging first. add circuit-breaker to auto-unflag if >1% error delta.
leah: telemetry needs an extra dimension: `auth.attribution_source` = {header, token_claim, fallback}. without that we can't tell when fallback happened. i can add sampling in the auth layer to tag 1% of requests with provenance if we can't change everything now.
sophie: good. also need a console UI change: show both "client-reported project" and "auth-resolved project" in the request detail page. ops and CS keep getting confused.
aj: config snippet i was thinking of for the strict mode:
```yaml
auth:
  routing_priority: [project, org]
  fallback_behavior: strict  # options: strict | permissive
```
leah: for rollout plan: 1) add telemetry tag and dashboard panel (auth.attribution_source) 2) enable strict mode behind flag in canary 3) monitor quota deltas and 5xxs for 24h 4) migrate customers with multipart uploads if needed 5) flip globally.
nate: who owns the(console UI change? i can pick up the small diff to show both fields, should be ~2 dev days.
sophie: assign to nate for UI, leah for telemetry & auth sampling, aj for rollout flag + revert code. i'll create a quick runbook for CS: how to spot these cases and contact eng.
ops-bot: alert created: #inc-1778889999 — auth attribution mismatch; owners (sophie, aj, leah). runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-attribution-fallback
sophie: thanks — let's triage in the 30m sync, i'll include a short customer note draft for CS.
aj: small note — we'll also add an event in audit logs when fallback is used: `auth.fallback=true` so SRE can correlate.
leah: adding that to telemetry plan. will post progress in this thread.
sophie: cool. if anyone finds evidence of tokens being reissued incorrectly, ping me immediately.
